name: responsibility
description: What the subject element is responsible for, in one plain sentence the LLM worded from the facts its request showed (knowledge-build epic, section 11.4): a deployable unit, component, data store, destination, external system or person. The value is the document kind it is worded for, c4. Of origin llm, the role that wrote it; a reworded sentence is a new observation of the same claim.

basis.description: evidenced when it cites what people wrote: a README or document claim, Javadoc in a cited excerpt, or an evidenced summary; else inferred.

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: intent
description: What the subject does with the other end of one of its interactions and why, in a phrase of 3 to 8 words starting with a verb, worded by the LLM (knowledge-build epic, section 11.4). The value is the claim ID of the interaction: a link between containers, a line between components, or a person's use of a unit. Of origin llm.

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: summary
description: What a type, package, Maven module or repository is for and how it works, in a few sentences the LLM wrote from its facts, source code and the summaries of the units it contains (knowledge-build epic, section 11.3). The value is the unit's level: type, package, module or repo. Later roles read it in place of whole files; its confidence comes from the share of sentences the checks kept. Of origin llm, the role that wrote it; a reworded summary is a new observation of the same claim.

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

sentences.description: The kept sentences, in order, each with the facts it cites (a contained summary's citation resolved to the facts that summary cites).

items.description: One sentence: its text, without citations, and cites, the IDs of the facts it cites.

basis.description: Of the first sentence, on what the unit is for: evidenced when it cites what people wrote (a README claim, Javadoc in a cited excerpt, or an evidenced summary); else inferred.

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: flow-significance
description: Whether the subject flow is worth drawing in one scope's documents, judged by the LLM from the traced candidate flows of that scope, one for each shape (knowledge-build epic, section 11.5; ADR 0108). The value is the scope: system, or the repository whose documents draw it. Of origin llm; a new judgement of the same flow and scope is a new observation of the same claim.

category.description: What kind of flow it is.

rank.description: Of a significant flow, its place in the order a reader sees them, from 1.

model.description: The model that judged it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

content.description: The content hash of the flow's steps the judgement holds for.

name: flow-narrative
description: The title, walkthrough and pre- and post-conditions of the subject flow, worded by the LLM from its steps, the responsibilities of the units it crosses and the intents of its interactions (knowledge-build epic, section 11.5; ADR 0108). The value is the document kind it is worded for, c4. Of origin llm; a reworded narrative is a new observation of the same claim.

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

title.description: At most 6 words naming the business scenario.

walkthrough.description: Two to four sentences of what the flow does, without citations.

preconditions.description: What must hold before it starts.

fieldCites.description: The facts each of walkthrough, preconditions and postconditions cites: an array of fact IDs by field.

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

content.description: The content hash of the flow's steps the narrative holds for.

name: purpose
description: What the system as a whole is for, in one plain sentence of 8 to 29 words the LLM worded from its units' and people's responsibilities, its external systems, its main flows' titles and its READMEs' claims (knowledge-build epic, section 11.6; ADR 0109). The subject is the system; the value is the document kind it is worded for, c4. Of origin llm; a reworded purpose is a new observation of the same claim.

cites.description: The facts it cites, an earlier answer standing for the facts it cites.

basis.description: evidenced when it cites a README claim; else inferred (ADR 0060).

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: key-fact
description: The single fact about how the system is built that a new reader most needs, such as how its parts communicate, where its data lives or what everything depends on, in one plain sentence of 8 to 35 words the LLM worded from the same inputs as the purpose (knowledge-build epic, section 11.6; ADR 0109). The subject is the system; the value is the document kind, c4. Of origin llm.

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

cites.description: The facts it cites, an earlier answer standing for the facts it cites.

basis.description: evidenced when it cites a README claim; else inferred (ADR 0060).

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: lead-verdict
description: Investigate's verdict on the subject lead (knowledge-build epic, section 11.2, Mode A; ADR 0110): the value is confirmed, refuted or unclear. Of origin llm; its lineage is the lead's claim, so it ends with the lead. A refuted lead stays stored, so it is not asked again until what it points at changes.

title.description: For a confirmed lead, the risk's title.

finding.description: The verdict's justification: what the cited code shows.

names.description: The identifiers it rests on, as the code writes them, each in the lines it cites.

cites.description: The file ranges it cites, as repo:path:from-to, each verified to hold its names.

basis.description: Whether it rests on what people wrote: evidenced when it cites a README or document claim, else inferred from code and configuration (#753).

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

reason.description: Why the verdict is unclear when the model gave none: the lead was not answered, or its answer was rejected twice.

name: investigated-risk
description: A risk Investigate found and Lantern verified (knowledge-build epic, section 11.2; ADR 0110): a confirmed lead, or a risk it found exploring a unit or the system. The subject is its first unit; the value is its key: when it confirms leads, their kind, a space and their units sorted and joined by commas (the confirmed leads of one kind on the same units are one risk, #747), else its names sorted and joined by commas, so a reworded rerun is a new observation of the same risk. Of origin llm, shown as found by the LLM.

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

finding.description: What the code does, in one or two sentences.

consequence.description: What can happen because of it, in one or two sentences.

impact.description: What an attacker or a failure could do to data or availability.

lead.description: The lead it confirms, if any.

names.description: The identifiers it rests on, as the code writes them, each in the lines it cites.

cites.description: The file ranges it cites, as repo:path:from-to, each verified to hold its names.

mode.description: Which Investigate mode found it: checking leads, exploring a unit, or the whole system.

basis.description: Whether it rests on what people wrote: evidenced when it cites a README or document claim, else inferred from code and configuration (#753).

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: finding-wording
description: Investigate's wording of a finding a fixed check raised, the subject (knowledge-build epic, section 11.2, Merging with static findings; ADR 0110): a risk it found that restates the finding is stored here, never as a second risk. The value is the risk's key. Of origin llm; its lineage is the finding's claim and the lead's.

support.description: The support judge's verdict on the text against its cited inputs, when it checked it (knowledge-build epic, section 11.7; ADR 0101): its confidence was multiplied by 1, 0.8 or 0.5.

consequence.description: What can happen because of it.

lead.description: The lead it confirms, if any.

mode.description: Which Investigate mode found it: checking leads, exploring a unit, or the whole system.

basis.description: Whether it rests on what people wrote: evidenced when it cites a README or document claim, else inferred from code and configuration (#753).

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: INVESTIGATED_CONNECTION
description: A connection Investigate found and Lantern verified that no static or resolved link states (knowledge-build epic, section 11.2; ADR 0110): the subject unit uses the object, a model element or a new external system or database. Its key is its two ends and its interaction. Of origin llm, drawn as a line marked found by the LLM; sequence flows are not traced through it.

description.description: What the unit uses it for, in a phrase.

technology.description: The technology, if the code shows it.

names.description: The identifiers it rests on, as the code writes them, each in the lines it cites.

cites.description: The file ranges it cites, as repo:path:from-to, each verified to hold its names.

mode.description: Which Investigate mode found it: checking leads, exploring a unit, or the whole system.

basis.description: Whether it rests on what people wrote: evidenced when it cites a README or document claim, else inferred from code and configuration (#753).

model.description: The model that wrote it, as provider/model.

answer.description: The stored answer it comes from: its fingerprint in the answer cache, which names the role, prompt version, model and inputs of the request (#753).

name: not-asked
description: A role did not ask the model about the subject, the item's subject, or got no answer for it (knowledge-build epic, sections 10 and 12; #741): a budget refused it, the request failed, or the item was missing from the answer twice. The value is the role. Of origin llm; the unknowns page lists them, and the next run asks again.

item.description: The item's subject as the role names it, when it is not an entity ID.

name: not-investigated
description: Investigate did not look at the subject, a deployable unit or the system (knowledge-build epic, section 11.2, Failure; ADR 0110): a budget refused it, the provider failed, or the model cannot use tools. The value is investigate. Of origin llm; the findings say which were left out.
